title: Example 14-8: Two Paragraphs of Verse Stage Directions

illustrates.quote: Stage Directions between Lines of Verse Dialogue a. Use 7-7 margins for stage directions or cues. b. Use 9-7 margins for additional paragraphs of stage directions.

blocks.text: Give me the gown. Where is thy instrument?

print.notes: BRUTUS is printed as a left-flush speaker label on its own line, with the verse dialogue indented below it (the given braille merges name and first line onto one 1-cell line, no separator, per 14.1.6/14.6.1a); two consecutive italicised stage-direction paragraphs follow, unenclosed, the second an 'additional paragraph' (14.6.3b); a further verse line by BRUTUS follows as a same-speaker continuation.
print.printFeatures: Left-aligned bold speaker name with indented verse dialogue beneath it; two paragraphs of italicised, unenclosed stage directions interrupt the verse.

braille.notes: Line 1: verse dialogue at 1-5(effectively 1-cell here, a single short line) margins (14.6.1a). Line 2: stage direction at 7-7 margins (14.6.3a), NO blank line before or after (14.6.3d, reusing 14.5.3d's own wording for verse). Line 3: an additional stage-direction paragraph at 9-7 margins (14.6.3b), again no surrounding blank line. Line 4: BRUTUS's own continuation verse line at 3-5 margins (14.6.1b), again with no blank line separating it from the stage direction above.

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on print substance (A's own speaker+items/text shapes were both reduced to this schema's own {kind:'speech'}/{kind:'stage-direction'} convention, matching example-14-6/14-9's own precedent). Forward-translated through Emboss's translator (alternating {type:'play',subtype:'verse'} and {type:'stage'} blocks, matching margins): the CONTENT and MARGINS of all four lines match exactly, but Emboss inserts a spurious blank line both before AND after each stage-direction block, directly contradicting 14.6.3d/14.5.3d's 'do not insert blank lines ... between the lines of dialogue' — traced to document.mjs's own `poemRunBoundaries`: a 'stage' block is neither a verse block nor a recognised stanza separator, so it breaks the surrounding verse run into two isolated single-line 'poems', each of which then gets F-121's own blank-line-before/after-a-poem treatment. This is a genuine, newly-documented Emboss gap (F-240, standards-findings.md), specific to the VERSE case (the PROSE case, example-14-6, is unaffected — a non-verse 'play' block never enters this run-boundary logic at all) — EXPECTED MISMATCH, not a gold-file error (see differences.md).
